summary: rescanLyrics leaks worker goroutines forever when a SetTrackLyrics write errors mid-scan
scenario: Admin triggers POST /api/boards/{id}/rescan-lyrics on a large board. A transient DB error on any SetTrackLyrics returns 500 and abandons the `for res := range results` loop. The 8 worker goroutines (and the jobs producer) are now blocked forever on `results <- ...` / `jobs <- ...` (unbuffered channels, no reader); wg.Wait() never returns, close(results) never runs. Every failed rescan permanently leaks up to ~9 goroutines + their tracks, an unbounded resource leak driving the process toward OOM.
suggested_fix: Drain the results channel to completion instead of returning early: collect errors into a var, keep ranging until the channel closes, then respond once. Or give the worker sends a select on r.Context().Done() so they unblock on request cancellation.

summary: aiBuild destroys the existing layout before rebuilding and aborts mid-loop on error, leaving the board in a corrupt/half-applied state
scenario: Any AddColumn/PlaceTrack failure part-way through the loop returns 500 after the old layout has ALREADY been wiped (RemoveColumn loop) and Cols set to len(cats). The board is left with some columns rebuilt, some missing, tracks partially placed, and Cols mismatching the real column count. There is no transaction/rollback, so a single mid-operation error permanently corrupts a previously-good board. RemoveColumn/UpdateBoardCols errors are also swallowed (`_ =`).
suggested_fix: Perform the clear+rebuild inside a single store transaction so a failure rolls back to the prior layout; at minimum stop discarding the old layout until the new one is fully committed, and don't ignore RemoveColumn/UpdateBoardCols errors.

summary: attachBoard passes an unchecked board to engine.ReloadBoard and half-commits on load failure
scenario: If LoadBoardByID returns (nil, nil) for a non-existent/empty board (no not-found branch here, unlike getBoard), ReloadBoard(nil) is handed a nil *game.Board and can nil-deref/panic in the engine. Separately, when LoadBoardByID errors the DB attach has already committed but the engine is never reloaded — persistent state and live game state diverge with no rollback.
suggested_fix: After LoadBoardByID, check `board == nil` and return 404 before calling ReloadBoard; consider ordering the engine reload so a load failure doesn't leave a committed-but-unapplied attach (or make attach+reload atomic).

summary: decodeJSON reads request bodies with no size limit (no http.MaxBytesReader) on every POST/PATCH endpoint
scenario: A client with the admin secret (or any request before the decode-side validation runs) POSTs a multi-gigabyte JSON body to e.g. POST /api/boards or POST /api/boards/{id}/tracks. json.Decoder buffers/allocates without bound, exhausting server memory (memory DoS). Field-length checks (name<=200 etc.) only run AFTER the whole body is decoded, so they provide no protection.
suggested_fix: Wrap the body once: `r.Body = http.MaxBytesReader(w, r.Body, 1<<20)` (or pass a limit into decodeJSON) before decoding; optionally dec.DisallowUnknownFields().

summary: CORSHandler sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * on all admin responses, allowing any web origin to call/read the admin API
code:
w.Header().Set("Access-Control-Allow-Origin", "*")
w.Header().Set("Access-Control-Allow-Methods", "GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS")
w.Header().Set("Access-Control-Allow-Headers", "Authorization, Content-Type")
scenario: Any website an attendee visits can issue cross-origin requests to the admin API and read the responses. Auth here is a bearer header (not a cookie) and Allow-Credentials is NOT set, so this is not a drive-by CSRF: a malicious page cannot forge the Authorization header without already knowing the secret. Residual risk is limited to origin-agnostic probing/response-reading if the secret leaks, but the blanket wildcard on a secret-gated admin surface is broader than necessary for a fixed set of first-party origins (stage/mobile/admin).
suggested_fix: Reflect an allow-list of known first-party origins instead of '*'; keep Allow-Credentials unset. If '*' is intentional for a header-token API, document it — but do not add Allow-Credentials while using '*'.

summary: Raw err.Error() from the store is returned verbatim in 500 responses across every handler, leaking internal/SQL detail
scenario: Any store error (DB down, constraint violation, query error) is echoed straight to the client. An authenticated admin — or anyone who has obtained the secret — sees raw Postgres error text: table/column names, constraint names, driver internals. This is repeated in every handler (boards.go, layout.go, tracks.go, aibuild.go). Gated by auth, so impact is limited, but it exposes schema internals to the client and logs.
suggested_fix: Log the real error server-side and return a generic message (e.g. http.Error(w, "internal error", 500)) to the client for all 500 paths.

summary: placeTrack does not validate `pos`, nor that `col` is within the board's actual column count, allowing phantom-column placements and negative ordering
scenario: col is only bounded to 1-8, not to the board's real Cols (unlike addColumn which fetches the board). Placing a track at col=8 on a 2-column board writes a placement into a column that does not exist, corrupting the layout. body.Pos is taken directly from JSON with no bounds check (negative or huge), and the decode error is discarded, so ordering can be set to arbitrary/negative values depending on store behavior.
suggested_fix: Fetch the board and reject col > board.Cols with 400/409; validate pos into a sane range (e.g. 0..rows-1); do not silently ignore the decode error.

summary: renameCategory accepts an unbounded category string (no length cap), inconsistent with addColumn's 100-char limit
scenario: PATCH /api/boards/{id}/columns/{col} with a multi-megabyte `category` string is accepted and persisted (addColumn caps this at 100 chars, renameCategory does not). Combined with the missing body size limit (adminapi-4), this lets a caller bloat board storage and later payloads with oversized category names.
suggested_fix: Add the same `len(body.Category) > 100` check used in addColumn.
